sources.README.md:
# Laboratory microscopy series upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Node 22.23.2.
Dependencies: Vue 3.4.38; jsdom 22.1.0; esbuild 0.21.5. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

The mounted component delegates synchronous select/retry/hide commands to its
session, projects state through the actual framework, and disposes its session
on lifecycle teardown. The source uses EventTarget and AbortController; decode
may return a value or Promise. jQuery commands use synchronous triggerHandler.

sources.src/Workspace.vue:
<template><section data-business="Laboratory sequence transfer"><output>{{ owner.fileId || 'closed' }}:{{ owner.attemptId || 0 }}</output></section></template>
<script>
import {shallowRef,onBeforeUnmount} from 'vue3';
import {Session} from './session.js';
export default {props:['host'],setup(props){const owner=shallowRef({}),session=new Session(props.host,s=>{owner.value=s;});onBeforeUnmount(()=>session.dispose());return {owner,select:f=>session.select(f),retry:()=>session.retry(),hide:()=>session.hide(),dispose:()=>session.dispose(),snapshot:()=>session.snapshot()};}};
</script>

public_inputs.task:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

limitations: Applies when a source can emit synchronously during start, decoding can finish asynchronously out of arrival order, and display validity has a documented lifecycle identity; it does not establish policy for rejected decodes or transfer completion.

Arrival tokens must be scoped to the business display lifecycle. In this source, README.md states: "Retry replaces the physical attempt without\nopening another visit." Therefore retry keeps the visit ordering domain, while selecting even the same file creates a new one.
This guidance preserves decoded-frame audit history even when display becomes stale. A different product that explicitly discards stale results requires a separate boundary policy.

rules.body:
Apply this pattern when startup may publish cached events synchronously and asynchronous decoding can reorder their completions. TASK states: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives." and "Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward." README.md confirms: "start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order."

Establish an idempotent listener-removal capability and register the listener before invoking source start. Removal must commit its inert/removed state before calling the underlying detach operation, because README.md states: "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;\nthat callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is\ninert." After start returns, recheck cancellation because synchronous callbacks may have invalidated the attempt before its handle was returned.

Assign a strictly increasing token when each packet arrives, before decoding it. Audit every successfully decoded frame independently, then paint only if the exact display lifecycle remains current, the physical attempt is not cancelled, and the token is newer than the last painted token. This separates arrival order from decode completion order and prevents an older continuation from overwriting newer display state.

Scope arrival and displayed-order state to the visit rather than file identity or physical attempt identity: README.md states, "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without\nopening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." Use attempt cancellation as an additional paint guard so obsolete retry attempts cannot paint, while the visit token prevents rollback across attempts in the same visit.

Preserve history independently of painting. src/session.js identifies the two effects as "audit:frame=>this.host.recordProgress?.({fileId:v.file.id,attemptId:n,frame})" and "this.host.showProgress?.({fileId:v.file.id,attemptId:n,frame})"; README.md states: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." A stale decoded frame may still be audited even when it must not repaint.

Treat the newest eligible decoded frame as a full replacement rather than enforcing numeric monotonicity. README.md states: "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Only arrival tokens are monotonic.

Keep unrelated consumers unchanged when their ordering contract differs. TASK requires: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,\nand subsequent uses." README.md says telemetry's "existing live delta observations are separate\nfrom the panel." Therefore do not change collectProgressTelemetry startup/listener ordering as part of the panel repair.

Preserve transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, notices, and queue-record shape. TASK requires restoration "without changing the public\ntransfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior." README.md fixes queue records as "{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}" absent separate authorization.

Verify at least: a cached packet emitted synchronously by start is decoded, audited, and displayed; multiple startup packets with reversed decode completion paint only the newest arrival while auditing both; a newer full frame may decrease the displayed value; showProgress re-entry that selects, hides, or disposes during start leaves cleanup usable and prevents obsolete painting; retry preserves visit identity but cancels old-attempt painting; selecting the same file creates a new display lifecycle; repeated removal is inert; telemetry and subsequent shared-source uses remain unchanged. Run public JavaScript/Vue syntax or build checks with generated output outside the submitted workspace.

checkpoints: On attempt startup, install the panel progress listener before invoking the progress source's start method so synchronously emitted cached packets are observed.
Establish the attempt's cleanup/removal capability before start can synchronously emit callbacks and re-enter select, hide, or dispose.
Assign an arrival-order token when each panel packet is received, before decoding begins.
Always append the decoded frame to transfer history through recordProgress, including frames whose decode completes after a newer packet.
Paint a decoded frame only if its visit is still current and no newer-arriving packet has already become the displayed frame.
Keep the telemetry consumer's existing start/listen and live-delta behavior unchanged.
After the Action, run the public JavaScript/Vue syntax or build checks without placing generated artifacts in the workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not change public transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, cancellation, audit, notice, or queue-record behavior beyond restoring the missing initial panel progress and preventing stale display rollback.
Do not suppress audit/history recording merely because a frame is stale for display.
Do not make loaded values monotonic; a newer full frame is allowed to decrease or reset the displayed value.
Do not conflate a retry attempt with a new visit.
Do not conflate selecting the same file object again with the prior visit.
Do not add byteCount to queue records without separate authorization.
Do not change collectProgressTelemetry behavior while repairing the panel consumer.
Do not allow a callback from an obsolete visit, cancelled attempt, hidden panel, or disposed workspace to repaint the current panel.
Do not make repeated cleanup/removal observable after the first removal.
Do not modify tests or configuration, and do not place compiled output or caches in the submitted workspace.
lifecycle_identity: A workspace Session has its own lifetime and becomes permanently disposed after dispose.
A selection creates a visit identified by visitId; selecting the same file object again creates a distinct visit.
A retry retains the current visit identity but creates a new physical attempt identified by attemptId.
The file object and source are shared across attempts and visits for that file, so file identity alone is insufficient to decide whether a decoded result may paint.
Panel display validity is tied to the exact current visit and the newest eligible packet arrival within that display lifecycle.
Each physical attempt owns its AbortController and cancellation state.

obligations.text: Restore the warm-source initial panel progress update by making the panel listener able to receive packets emitted synchronously by start.
For the panel consumer, order display eligibility by packet arrival rather than asynchronous decode completion, so completion of an older packet cannot overwrite a frame from a newer packet.
Treat decoded frames as full replacements: the newest eligible frame may legitimately decrease or reset loaded values.
Continue recording transfer progress history for decoded panel packets independently of whether each frame remains eligible to paint.
Ensure synchronous showProgress/onState re-entry during start can select, hide, or dispose safely even though the outer caller has not yet received the attempt handle.
Retain existing cancellation and cleanup semantics: removal takes effect before any synchronous host detach re-entry, repeated removal is inert, and obsolete attempts cannot subsequently paint.
Preserve visit and attempt semantics across select and retry, including queue record shape and existing notice behavior.
Leave diagnostic collectProgressTelemetry live-delta observations and subsequent source uses unchanged.
Keep the mounted Vue component's synchronous command delegation, framework state projection, and teardown disposal behavior unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Panel listener registration and usable cleanup state must be established before feed.start can synchronously emit progress.
Packet arrival order must be captured before feed.decode, because decode may return immediately or later and completions may reorder.
A decoded frame's audit append must remain independent from the later display-validity decision.
Before painting, the continuation must verify both current visit validity and that no newer-arriving eligible frame has superseded it.
Listener removal must be committed before invoking any synchronous host detach callback or allowing re-entrant lifecycle commands.
Cancellation or lifecycle invalidation occurring during synchronous start must be observed before createAttempt returns and before any later decode continuation may paint.
preservation: Ordinary asynchronous streaming continues to decode, audit, and display eligible frames.
recordProgress remains the transfer-history path; showProgress remains the open-panel painting path.
Queue records retain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
Retry replaces the physical attempt without creating another visit.
Selecting the same file object again creates a new visit.
Queue notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, hide, disposal, and component teardown retain existing behavior.
Telemetry remains separate from panel display and preserves its existing live delta observations.
A shared source remains reusable across attempts and visits.
Host callbacks remain synchronous unless explicitly deferred.
Rejected decode and physical transfer completion remain outside this embedding's modeled behavior.
scope: Business code relevant to panel progress composition in /workspace/src/session.js, with src/Workspace.vue inspected only to preserve its public component behavior.
The maintenance window covers synchronous cached packets emitted by a progress source during start and asynchronous decode completions that can arrive out of order.
No tests, configuration, dependency metadata, scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests are in scope.

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Node 22.23.2.
Dependencies: Vue 3.4.38; jsdom 22.1.0; esbuild 0.21.5. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

The mounted component delegates synchronous select/retry/hide commands to its
session, projects state through the actual framework, and disposes its session
on lifecycle teardown. The source uses EventTarget and AbortController; decode
may return a value or Promise. jQuery commands use synchronous triggerHandler.
